correctness.rationale: An MMD pair can only be strongly resolved by one of its endpoints: a geodesic from a third resolving vertex would extend past an endpoint and produce a neighbor farther from the other endpoint. Conversely any shortest path can be extended as a contiguous subpath to a maximal geodesic, whose endpoints are MMD; a cover then resolves the original pair. Thus sdim=50-alpha(R). I independently reconstructed distances by simultaneous shortest-path relaxation from the two layer representatives, recovered the frozen distance rows and checked all 1225 pairs for mutual maximality. R has only the outer steps ±5,±7,±9,±11,±12 and inner steps ±9,±11 (125 and 50 edges). In the outer component rotate a nonempty independent set to contain 0: its 14 other available indices are partitioned into the five exhibited cliques, giving at most six. In the inner component the cycles t+9j for j=0,...,4 and t=0,5,10,15,20 close by an allowed step and partition the vertices (9 is invertible modulo 5); each supplies at most two independent vertices. The displayed witnesses realize both bounds. An independent take-or-skip bitset recurrence also gave independence numbers 6 and 10, and the complement directly resolved all 1225 pairs. The 2015 prediction comparison is correct; the published upper bound is not contradicted. The 2017 formulation is a bibliographic detail with the access limitation below.
